terms.definition: The IG's own build timestamp, verbatim from `package.manifest.json`. Not reformatted: a transcription that normalises is no longer a transcription.
The canonical base every artefact's canonical URL extends, e.g. `http://hl7.org/fhir/uv/ips`.
Instance id — the directory this index lives in, e.g. `<ig>`.

The IG API hub: the region of the IG's hub page between the two markers its post-processing writes after the Publisher has run (`ig-api.html` between `IG_API_HUB_START` and `IG_API_HUB_END` by default; an overlay whose post-processing uses other names passes them to the ingest). `url` is the page it was read from; `localPath` is the fragment, held so a page can fetch it (bean `680p`) rather than retype its prose — as a JSON node (`{ from, between, html }`), because an `.html` fragment published in the served graph would be a page with no <body>. Absent means the IG publishes no hub, or it was not materialised.

The IG's own `package.tgz` — every resource's JSON in one file, as the Publisher packaged it. Held (`--materialize-package`) so a page can fetch the one archive and read a resource out of it in the browser, rather than this graph copying hundreds of resource files (bean `680p`, `visualizer-loading`). Absent means not held.
NPM-style package id, e.g. `hl7.fhir.uv.ips`.

Sidecars an enumeration listed that bound to no artefact. Absent means none; an empty array is not written. See {@link UnboundSidecarSchema} for why these are recorded rather than warned about and forgotten.
FHIR canonical URL. Absent for examples and instances; see the doc above.
Editorial grouping from `artifacts.html`. Absent means the IG published no artefact page.

The resource's own `code` when it is a concept (`Basic.code`, a CodeableConcept; `Questionnaire.code`, a list of Codings, kept as the codings with no text). A string `code` (SearchParameter's) is a computable name, not a concept, and is not this. Copied, never looked up: a coding with no display stays without one.
Stable within the index: `<resourceType>/<id>`, which is unique where a bare id is not.

Position on the Publisher's `artifacts.html`, 0-based, first appearance. The category's order and the artefact's order within it are both read off this — a renderer that must match the Publisher's page (owner, 2026-10-01: every phase renders equivalent to the standard IG render) has no other source for either. Absent exactly when `category` is.

The resource's own `meta.profile`: the profiles it says it conforms to, as written. An instance has no canonical, title or description of its own, and this and `code` are what it does state; a list that showed neither showed an empty row. Absent when the resource claims none.
The URI the artefacts are published AT — what a `published` URL is resolved against.
When the source was read. An index with no read date cannot be told from a current one.
Git revision of the branch read, when the source was a checkout. Absent means not established.
`artifacts.html` — the ONLY source of an artefact's editorial category.
`canonicals.json` — the spine for anything with a canonical URL.
`package.tgz` -> `package/.index.json` — the spine for everything else. Lossy; see the module doc.
`package.manifest.json` — package id, version, FHIR version, build date.
The IG API enumeration schemas, when present.
Canonical URLs of the artefacts whose terms this context binds, where that could be established.
Instance-relative path, present iff these bytes were materialised.
Number of codes, for a ValueSet.
`schemas/<name>.displays.json` — display strings, keyed by code.
`<name>.jsonld` — the JSON-LD vocabulary, published at the IG ROOT, not under `schemas/`.
`schemas/<name>.openapi.json` — this ARTEFACT's OpenAPI fragment. Never `openapi/openapi.json`; see the module doc.
Number of properties, for a logical model.
`schemas/<name>.schema.json` — the JSON Schema for this artefact.
Which enumeration listed it.
The sidecar file the enumeration named.
Why no artefact matched: the strategies tried, in order.
Its title, as the enumeration gives it — usually the only human handle on what was missed.
Column keys shown before a row is opened. Default: the first six.
The annex, relative to the directory that holds this declaration.
The page file under `input/pagecontent/`, e.g. `dictionary.md`.
`local`: a copy this site serves; `upstream`: the file where the IG publishes it.
The cache branch the commit was read from, for the reader; the commit is what is fetched.
The IG instance, as `index.lock.json` names it.
The repository the cache branch lives in: the IG's own.
The pinned cache commit.
The IG commit the AST says it was compiled from (`manifest.json` `inputs.sourceRevision`), when it says.
What the AST is valid for, in `CompiledInputsSchema`'s shape.
What stays provisional until a full Publisher run.
On a merged (mixed-provenance) AST: the revision that built this resource.
The resource's JSON file, relative to the AST directory.
The IG source file it was built from, where known.
`shape` — the layers agree the token exists and disagree about what KIND of value it holds, so a consumer substituting one into the other's rule emits something invalid.

Where it was seen. `min(1)` rather than `min(2)`: a `shape` conflict needs two layers by definition, but a `malformed` value needs only one, and requiring two would have made the second kind unrepresentable in the schema written to hold it.
The repository the bytes were read from.
The `fhir.template` package name, e.g. `who.template.root`.
The stylesheet within that repository.
The commit they were read at. Provenance.
Its declared version, e.g. `0.5.0`.
The package the rule was read from.
The selector, verbatim, e.g. `#ig-status.ig-status-draft`.

The chain's TOP layer — the template package an IG names — e.g. `who.template.root`. v1 put the id of the IG it was ingested beside here; v2 keys the chrome by the template, because every IG building with that chain wears it. An IG's own id and status are `ig-identity.json`'s.
The chain, BASE FIRST, so index order is override order.
The top layer's version, e.g. `0.5.0`.
The package whose declaration wins.
The custom property, including its leading `--`.
Lower layers this shadows, nearest first. Empty when only one declared it.
The winning value, verbatim.
Repository-relative POSIX paths. A trailing `/` marks a directory.
The IG's `id` from `sushi-config.yaml`; SUSHI's `packageId` defaults to it.
When it was read. A status is a fact at a moment, not forever.
Where it was read: a repository and file, so the claim can be re-checked.
`draft`, `active`, `retired` … — what selects the template's watermark.
Set when the group itself is a page rather than only a container.
Its `canonical`, the base every `href` is relative to.
The IG's `id` from `sushi-config.yaml`, e.g. `hl7.fhir.uv.ips`.
The repository the config was read from.
The path within that repository.
The commit it was read at. Provenance.
The IG's canonical URL, where it declares one.
The NPM-style package id, e.g. `who.smart.trust`.
The IG version this harvest was taken at. An id alone collides across versions.
When the harvest ran.
The published site or package the exports were read out of.
A URL for the harvest run, if one exists.
The commit the tag points at, where GitHub reports it.
The release's page on GitHub.
When they were read (UTC date). A release made later is not here until the next read.
Newest first, as GitHub lists them. Drafts are never recorded: they are not published.
`owner/repo` the releases were read from.
`sha256:<hex>` as GitHub reports it; absent on assets uploaded before GitHub computed digests.
Where to fetch the bytes: GitHub's `browser_download_url`.
Clock for expiry, in epoch milliseconds (tests). Defaults to `Date.now`.
How long a determined result may be reused, in milliseconds.
Total reported by the first Bundle page, if present.
Active, non-expired FHIR R4 `Consent` resources returned by the registry.
ISO-8601 timestamp against which `provision.period` validity was evaluated.
Entries in the searchset `Bundle` that were filtered out (inactive, expired, not-yet-valid, informational `OperationOutcome`, etc.).
The initial ITI-108 search URL issued to the Consent Registry.
Action token(s).
Actor reference(s) (e.g. `"Practitioner/prac-1"` or `"Organization/org-1"`).
Base URL of the FHIR R4 Consent Registry (e.g. `"https://registry.example.org/fhir"`).
Category token(s) (e.g. `"http://loinc.org|59284-0"`).
Date filter(s), e.g. `"ge2026-01-01"`.
Custom `fetch` implementation (defaults to `globalThis.fetch`).
Follow `Bundle.link[relation="next"]` pagination links (defaults to `true`).
Optional HTTP headers (e.g. `{ Authorization: "Bearer ..." }`); no IUA claim is required.
Maximum number of Bundle pages to fetch when `followNext` is `true` (defaults to `10`).
Reference timestamp (`ISO-8601` string or `Date`) used to evaluate `provision.period` expiry (defaults to `new Date()`).
Patient reference (e.g. `"Patient/pat-1"` or `"pat-1"`).
Patient business identifier token (e.g. `"urn:oid:1.2.3|12345"`), sent as `patient.identifier`.
Profile canonical URL filter(s), sent as `_profile`.
PurposeOfUse token(s) (e.g. `"TREAT"`, `"HRESCH"`).
Security label token(s), sent as `security-label`.
Source reference filter, sent as `source-reference`.
Status parameter sent on the query (defaults to `"active"`).
Request timeout in milliseconds (defaults to `10_000`).
`"dropped"` when omitted entirely from the FHIR R5 Permission output; `"lossy"` when approximated in a FHIR R5 Permission element that does not preserve full ODRL semantics.
JSONPath-style location in the input ODRL Agreement or DCAT record.
Why FHIR R5 Permission has no exact home for this term, or how it was approximated.
The ODRL 2.2 (or DCAT 3 / SPDX) term name that has no exact FHIR R5 Permission home.
The input value that was dropped or only lossily approximated.
Optional display label for the agreement's fixed-version `uid` on `justification.evidence[0].display`.
Optional DCAT 3 `dcat:Resource` metadata for the agreement version.
Optional FHIR resource `id` for the rendered `Permission`.
Optional map from party/target IRIs (e.g. `"https://ministry-m.example.org/"`) to FHIR `Reference`s (e.g. `{ reference: "Organization/MinistryM" }` or display strings).
Optional human-readable display labels for HL7 `PurposeOfUse` codes.
Explicit `Permission.status` (`active | entered-in-error | draft | rejected`). If omitted, derived from `dcat["adms:status"]` when provided, or defaults to `"active"`.
Optional map from dataset/target IRIs to human-readable display labels on `rule.data.resource.reference.display`.
Every ODRL 2.2 (or DCAT 3 / SPDX) term from the input that has no exact home in FHIR R5 `Permission` (either omitted or only lossily approximated).
The rendered FHIR R5 `Permission` resource, validated against `FhirR5PermissionSchema`.
The version's ODRL policy; its `uid` is the fixed-version URL.
The fixed-version URL of the version this one amends (`dcat:previousVersion`).
Default ODRL action when `provision.action` is omitted (default: `"odrl:use"`).
ODRL profile URI written into `Set.profile` (default: {@link PCF_IG_CANONICAL}).
Prefix for minted policy `uid`s (default: `"urn:ihe:pcf:consent:"`).
Custom ODRL action graph (defaults to `ODRL_ACTIONS`).

Overarching implicit policy (`Policy-basic-normal`, `Policy-all-normal`, `Policy-break-glass-only`, `Policy-deny`, or a custom `PcfOdrlSet`) used when no active Consent is on file or when the Consent has expired (IHE PCF Volume 1 §1:53.2.1 & §1:53.4.2.5).
Requested ODRL action (defaults to `"odrl:use"`).
Requesting actor (FHIR reference such as `"Practitioner/ex-practitioner"`, DID, actor id, or `null`).
Groups or organizations the actor belongs to (e.g. `["Group/ex-privilegedUsers"]`).
Roles the actor holds (or group memberships).
Convenience shorthand: top-level `author` when `scope.author` is not passed.
Convenience shorthand: top-level `dataPeriod` / `dataDateTime` when `scope.dataPeriod` is not passed.
Convenience shorthand: top-level `dateTime` when `scope.dateTime` is not passed.
Convenience shorthand: top-level `encounter` when `scope.encounter` is not passed.
Convenience shorthand: top-level `purpose` when `scope.purpose` is not passed.
Request context: `purpose`, `dateTime`, `target`, `securityLabel`, `dataPeriod`, `author`, `encounter`.
Convenience shorthand: top-level `securityLabel` when `scope.securityLabel` is not passed.
Convenience shorthand: top-level `target` when `scope.target` is not passed.
Where in the table, e.g. `group[0].element[2].target[1]`.
